set.v: French and Spanish coin, amount not given
set.st: A Milwaukee Journal article of October 26, 1924 headlined "Is heiress to lost gold of Brisbois". Michel Brisbois (died 1837) was a Prairie du Chien fur trader of the Astor era. The 1924 feature tells the family legend: during an Indian scare he had a trusted voyageur row his French and Spanish coin out at night and drop it into the Mississippi, and a descendant in 1924 still hoped clam fishermen would bring it up. No spot in the river is given and nothing was ever recovered. LiDAR cache check (USGS 1 m, 2021): Nothing that fits the story stands out within the search area: the pits and lines it finds there are ditches, banks, ponds or natural ground. From the books: Michael Brisbois, at Prairie du Chien since 1781, ran the village bake-house (100 pounds of flour bought tickets for fifty loaves, which passed as small change with the Indians). The army seized his house and bake-house in 1816-17. He went blind in 1829 and at his death in 1837 was buried by his son on a prominent bluff behind the town. (WHS Coll. II, 1856 p. 125)
set.t: The pin is the Brisbois house (historic site, look-only); the drop point in the river is not given anywhere, so nothing goes on the low-water layer.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: 1924 syndicated feature retelling a c.1800 family legend, one source by the wire rule; river spot unknown
